mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate comparative statements of the form 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), preserving the direction of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says 'has N more' or 'has N fewer' compared to another person.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 more items than B' as A = 5, ignoring B's count.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: A direct count statement (e.g., 'A has N items') sets the current value of A to N at that point in the sequence, and later statements may modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a sentence that gives an explicit number for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating 'A has 10 items' as a permanent initial value that cannot change after later transfers.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the given order. Apply each transfer (including conditional transfers that depend on a comparison) immediately, updating both giver and receiver before any later statements that reference them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer or conditional transfer appears in the text.
mathgap.example: Delaying a transfer until after later statements, causing those statements to use the giver's old count.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For sentences equating two differences, translate them into the form (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of A and B'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting '(A - B) = (C - D)' as A = B + C - D, i.e., assigning only to A.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction) – Correct Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by multiplication (e.g., 'X increases by N times'), interpret it as X = X * N. When it says 'X decreases by N', interpret it as X = X - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering phrases like 'increases by N times' or 'decreases by N'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X increases by 2 times' as X = X + 2 instead of X = X * 2.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: If a group of people redistributes their items so that each ends up with the same amount, compute the total items among the group and divide by the number of people; assign that equal share to each.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says a group redistributes equally.
mathgap.example: Assuming redistribution leaves each person's original amount unchanged.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Gather every constraint implied by each statement, even those that do not directly involve the queried person, to build a complete system of equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: While parsing the problem, before solving.
mathgap.example: Skipping a relation between C and D because the question asks about E.

mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Treat both 'the number of X has more than Y' and 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as signed subtraction (X - Y), preserving the order of names, rather than as absolute values or direct assignments.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing any phrase that describes a difference between two persons.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B| (always non‑negative).

mathgap.title: Difference Equality Numeric Evaluation
mathgap.principle: When a difference equality (X - Y = A - B) involves variables whose values are already known, compute the numeric result and substitute it, simplifying the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After enough equations have been solved to know the values on both sides of a difference equality.
mathgap.example: Leaving (X - Y) = (A - B) unevaluated even though X, Y, A, B are known.

mathgap.title: Sum Constraint Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The combined quantity of X, Y, and Z is N' (or similar), translate it into the equation X + Y + Z = N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering statements that describe the total of a set of persons.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'The combined quantity of A, B, and C is 10' as A = 10 and B = C = 0.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Models default to thinking of ‘difference’ as magnitude rather than directional subtraction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of names and interpret the phrase as X - Y.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes the whole text as a static snapshot instead of respecting sequential updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, before processing later statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct assignments as immutable base values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow later transfers or other statements to modify the count after a direct assignment.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term (including assuming positivity).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model collapses (A - B) = (C - D) into A = B + C - D, losing the relational nature.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate the equality into a two‑sided equation and keep both sides intact.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increases by N times' as addition or division instead of multiplication.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase is ambiguous; the model defaults to additive interpretation.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'increases by N times' as multiplication (X = X * N).
